text.p: NYMEX crude oil fell to its lowest level in over a year, gold steady despite continued pressure on the silver price, while base metals were mainly firmer in London on Friday.
Jittery base metals markets probed higher, then turned back on Friday, a day after heavy fund liquidation sent prices tumbling on the London Metal Exchange.

Copper, aluminium and zinc, the worst hit in the selloff, had all logged some distance from Thursday's lows by the end of the morning rings, aided by drawdowns in London Metal Exchange (LME) inventories. But they reversed course, with copper at the helm, during the kerb.

Three months copper, which had tumbled some $60 to a low of $2,320 on Thursday by the late close, finished the morning kerb at $2,336 per tonne, down $4 from the previous kerb close. It turned back at a high of $2,349, after failing to pierce $2,350 resistance. Cash to threes backwardation, which flared by about $10 from morning levels to $50/$51 on a bout of borrowing in the rings, also narrowed. It was last indicated at $42/$47.

Aluminium also pared gains on the kerb, although it was holding on better than copper. Prices finished the kerb at $1,618, which was off the high of the day of $1,622 but still $9 stronger than Thursday's weak close.

Aluminium faced tough resistance at $1,625 and up after fund liquidation pushed it below the $1,630 support level on Thursday. Support was at $1,600. Still, a stock drop of 7,875 tonnes was supportive.
Zinc similarly was off highs but still in the plus column following the gloom of Thursday's selloff.
Aided by a 4,625 tonne stock drop, zinc had climbed to a high of $1,279 per tonne, but ended the kerb at $1,267, which was a gain of $8 from the previous kerb close.
Nickel was $10 easier at $7,620. But it had recovered from a test of the downside in the pre-market, when in it hit a low of $7,520. An inventory rise of 306 tonnes was shrugged off.

Tin, which alone was virtually unaffected by the sell-off, remained quiet and steady at $5,830/40, versus $5,850. Stocks were up 60 tonnes. Alloy was unchanged at $1,515 after a small 280-tonne stock decline.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures recovered slightly from early weakness Friday to end mostly higher, after silver led the complex lower for most of the week. COMEX May silver closed up 1.2 cents at $4.740 an ounce, after an inside-range-day, following the slump to a contract low at $4.655 Thursday. COMEX June gold ended up 30 cents at $351.80 an ounce, with the contract still seen trapped in the $350-355 range it has been in for the past month. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $348.50/00, compared to the London Friday afternoon fix at $347.40, and the New York close Thursday around $348.50/00.

Rainfall this week in some key hard red winter wheat areas of the U.S. Great Plains pressured CBOT soft red winter wheat futures to a lower close, traders said. Technicians said the wheat market broke this week on fund long liquidation. Sell-stops of up to 10 million bushels were hit in late and fast dealings Thursday, they said. Bearishness from a sharp, nearly limit-down move in soybean futures also spilled into the wheat market. Wheat closed 1-1/2 to 11 cents per bushel lower, with May down 3-1/4 at $3.71-3/4 a bushel. July closed down 1-1/2 cents at $3.71-1/2.

NEW YORK - NYMEX crude ended sharply lower Friday after the spot month fell below $19.00 a barrel for the first time in over a year as ample supply continued to hammer oil prices. May crude ended off 35 cents at $19.12 a barrel. May gasoline closed off 0.42 cent at 60.48 cents a gallon. May heating oil ended off 0.12 cent at 53.14 cents a gallon.
